issue: A busy flag prevents another capability helper entering, but alone cannot prevent an ordinary raw transaction alias from scheduling SQL while a role window is active. Do not claim that ordinary queries are guaranteed app_tenant merely because the count helper sets busy. Existing withTenantTx exposes its raw client to its callback; introducing a new privileged read must account for that alias/interleaving risk. No live exploit or test is claimed.
preferredSmallBoundary: Expose the count read as a closed operation receiving only Env, canonical OwnedStoreScope and validated pagination intent. That operation owns its withTenantTx internally and never returns/passes its transaction client, raw executor, callback or parent-ID batch to a caller. Its parent/owner/count/restore statements are fixed and awaited in one private callback; no caller can schedule ordinary SQL on that transaction during the window. The privileged part returns only scalar counts; the ordinary RLS parent metadata and page total are safe inputs to the existing adapter, which retains canonical shared projection assembly/validation. Root must approve the exact separation and names after the frozen393 source closure ends.
alternativeIfAdapterMustOwnRawTransactio: A guarded ordinary SQL facade and a private internal executor would have to reject all ordinary calls while a privileged window is active, including borrowed aliases and nested/reentrant operations. That is a larger shared transaction change and would require separately reviewed publisher compatibility/security gates; it is not part of a silent count-helper patch. Prefer the closed operation or choose paired RLS closure if the small boundary cannot satisfy the requirement.
qualificationAddition: Prove ordinary raw-client alias/interleaving cannot occur at the exported closed operation boundary, no client/callback/role/SQL/ID batch is accepted or leaked, and context restoration is verified before any data leaves. Test actual production route and controlled faults; no false assurance from helper-only busy tests.
disposition: Clarifies/tightens the pending proposal only. No infrastructure question to the user, no code grant assumed, no permission failure overridden.
